title: Build Reliable Gemini API Workflows
summary: Use the Google Gen AI SDK with environment-based credentials, configurable models, explicit conversation state, typed candidate handling, validation, bounded recovery, and privacy-safe evidence.
objectives: Explain Gemini API request, candidate, content-part, finish, safety, and usage contracts.
Use the Google Gen AI SDK with environment-based credentials and model configuration.
Own conversation state and validate candidate content before downstream use.
Classify API failures, retry safely, and preserve privacy-reviewed operational evidence.

sections.title: Treat responses as structured candidates
paragraphs: A Gemini content-generation request identifies a model, contents, and optional system instruction, generation, safety, tool, or output controls. A response can contain candidates, content parts, finish information, safety signals, citations or grounding metadata, and usage. Do not assume every success is one plain string.

Convenience text access is useful only after the workflow has checked the response contract. Inspect whether a candidate exists, which parts are present, why generation stopped, and whether safety or other conditions require a refusal, recovery, or escalation path.

code.label: Treat responses as structured candidates (Code Implementation)

sections.title: Configure credentials and models
paragraphs: Load GEMINI_API_KEY from the runtime environment or a managed secret store and fail closed when it is absent. Keep keys out of source, prompts, logs, client-side bundles, learner evidence, and screenshots; restrict, rotate, and revoke them according to current Google guidance.

Keep model identifiers, API version, output limits, timeout, retry budget, safety configuration, and storage decisions in reviewed configuration. Verify currently supported values and credentials for the actual Gemini API or Google Cloud deployment rather than assuming one setup fits every environment.

code.label: Secret-safe Gemini SDK boundary

sections.title: Own conversation state explicitly
paragraphs: Multi-turn chat helpers preserve or resend conversation history according to their SDK contract; they do not remove application responsibility. Define which user and model turns, files, tool results, summaries, and identifiers are retained and supplied on later requests.

Set truncation, summarization, branching, privacy, deletion, and recovery policy deliberately. A transcript shown in a UI, state held by a client object, and durable application records are different things and must not be conflated.

code.label: Own conversation state explicitly (Code Implementation)

sections.title: Validate finish, parts, and output
paragraphs: Route normal completion, output limits, safety blocks, recitation, malformed function calls, cancellation, and unknown finish outcomes separately using the current documented enums. Handle text, function requests, executable code, media, and other supported parts only when the workflow contract permits them.

Validate schemas, required evidence, citations, lengths, allowed values, and business rules before downstream use. Provider transport success, model completion, application validation, and external postcondition success are separate states.

code.label: Validate finish, parts, and output (Code Implementation)

sections.title: Recover and observe with bounds
paragraphs: Classify failures before retrying. Rate limits and transient service failures may use provider guidance, exponential backoff with jitter, maximum attempts, and an end-to-end deadline. Invalid arguments, permissions, blocked keys, unsupported models, and application validation failures require correction.

Record correlation, application and prompt versions, configured model reference, latency, usage, finish outcome, part types, validation, retry count, and terminal state under an allowlist. Exclude keys, authorization headers, sensitive raw content, and unnecessary provider identifiers.

code.label: Recover and observe with bounds (Code Implementation)

activity.title: Design and test a Gemini API client
instructions: Define a request contract with environment credentials, configurable model, system instruction, contents, output contract, timeout, retry budget, and trace identifier.
Document conversation-state ownership, retention, summarization, deletion, privacy, branching, and recovery behavior.
Implement or diagram handlers for normal text, safety block, output limit, unknown part, invalid output, authentication, permission, rate limit, timeout, cancellation, and service failure.
Use synthetic request/response fixtures so no paid call is required; prove every terminal path and a telemetry allowlist without exposing credentials or sensitive content.
evidence: A secret-free client implementation or design with typed candidate and part handling, state ownership, validation, bounded retries, and deterministic fixtures.
A state and telemetry record showing configuration versions, finish outcome, part types, usage, validation, retries, privacy controls, and terminal result.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which outcome in your client must be corrected or escalated instead of retried, and what evidence proves that decision?

cues.text: Treat Gemini responses as candidates with typed parts, finish information, safety signals, metadata, and usage instead of one trusted string.

cues.text: Ask learners what must be deleted when an SDK chat object and an application database both contain history.
Allow three minutes to classify authentication, rate-limit, safety-block, and timeout outcomes as correct, retry, reconcile, or escalate.
Check that every known finish, part, validation, and transport path reaches a bounded terminal state.
Guide the request contract, state policy, handlers, synthetic fixtures, and telemetry allowlist.
Begin the check after the learner can defend response structure, configuration, state, validation, recovery, and evidence.

questions.prompt: Why inspect candidates and parts before using response text?
choices: Responses can contain distinct finish outcomes, safety signals, and part types
Every response is a tool call
questions.explanation: Different response structures require different validation and terminal paths.

questions.prompt: Where should a reusable application obtain its model identifier?
choices: From reviewed configuration checked against current official documentation
questions.explanation: Model identifiers and capabilities change and must remain configurable.

questions.prompt: Who owns retention when an SDK chat helper tracks turns?
choices: The application and its documented data policy
The learner's browser in every deployment
questions.explanation: A helper does not replace application privacy, retention, deletion, and recovery responsibility.

questions.prompt: What should happen for an unsupported or unknown finish outcome?
choices: Enter an explicit safe failure or escalation path
questions.explanation: Unknown outcomes must not be silently accepted.

questions.prompt: Which failure should not be retried unchanged?
choices: An authentication, permission, or invalid-request failure
A provider-directed rate limit within budget
questions.explanation: Deterministic credential, authority, and request errors require correction.
